name: REMS Compliance
one_liner: Prescriber certification, patient enrollment, pharmacy qualification and dispensing controls.
fits_when: a product carries a REMS with elements to assure safe use, so only certified prescribers may prescribe it
each patient must be enrolled with a signed patient-prescriber agreement before the first dispense
only certified pharmacies may dispense, and each fill needs a dispense authorization
safe-use conditions such as a recent negative pregnancy test or lab value must be checked before dispensing
certifications expire and prescribers and pharmacies must recertify on a fixed cycle
the program owes the regulator periodic assessment reports and must track non-compliance
gives_you: Prescriber certification from training and knowledge assessment to signed attestation, review and recertification
Patient enrollment with a signed patient-prescriber agreement, risk category and monitoring results
Pharmacy qualification with an authorized representative, staff training and dispensing SOP attestation
Dispense authorizations checked against prescriber, patient, pharmacy and safe-use status, with a 7-day window
A REMS coordinator dashboard and patient 360 page with every test, authorization and status change
Row-level access so prescribers see only their patients and pharmacies only their own authorizations

catalogue.description: Run a REMS with elements to assure safe use. Prescribers train, pass the knowledge assessment and attest to certify; they enroll each patient with a signed agreement and log the required monitoring results. Pharmacies qualify through an authorized representative and request a dispense authorization before every fill, which is granted only when prescriber, patient, pharmacy and the latest safe-use test are all in good standing. The REMS coordinator reviews certifications, rules on authorizations and tracks non-compliance for assessment reports.

compliance: FDA REMS elements to assure safe use: certified prescribers, certified pharmacies and documented safe-use conditions
No dispense without a valid authorization issued against current certification and monitoring status
Patient data visible only to the enrolling prescriber and the REMS coordinator (HIPAA minimum necessary)
Audit trail and e-signatures on attestations and authorizations, aligned to 21 CFR Part 11
Non-compliance logged and trended for the REMS assessment report
catalogue.app_prompt_prefill: A pregnancy prevention REMS for one teratogenic oral therapy, covering about 2,400 certified prescribers and 600 pharmacies in the US. Prescribers certify after training and a knowledge assessment, enroll each patient with a signed patient-prescriber agreement and log monthly pregnancy tests. Pharmacies certify through an authorized representative and need a dispense authorization before every fill, issued only when prescriber, patient and pharmacy are in good standing and the latest negative test is under 7 days old. The REMS coordinator reviews non-compliance and prepares the FDA assessment reports.
